name: mycrew
description: A five-layer harness for Claude Code, each layer driving the one below: primitives and house rules, a pipeline that carries a task from decision to hardened code, a product plane holding what the product must do, and a chief on top that shapes the plane and dispatches its workers. On top, a watch that judges whether the work still serves what you asked for and stops what wandered. Install mycrew-tools first.

plugins.name: mycrew-tools
plugins.description: Layer 1/5 — the primitives. Small, project-agnostic skills you reach for mid-work: /slap resets a fix that has stopped working, /likec4 draws architecture as code, /reminder pins a rule as a hard constraint, /retract hunts down information declared wrong and cuts it out. Ships the house rule files too. Everything above builds on this.

plugins.name: mycrew-pipeline
plugins.description: Layer 2/5 — the build pipeline. Six stages carry one task from a decision to shipped code: /how-to-do settles the fork, /do builds it, then /refactor, /review, /secure and /test harden it. In review and secure, the eyes that hunt are never the author's. Every stage weighs what actually changed and skips in one honest line when the change doesn't earn it.

plugins.name: mycrew-product
plugins.description: Layer 3/5 — the product plane: everything true about the whole product, above the sub-projects. /product-init founds it. /braindump and /ask-me draw the product out of you and file each piece where it belongs; /propose-idea is the one that puts an idea in, and only on your approval. Whatever you affirm, wherever you affirm it, product-rules is the one rule set that decides where it lands and in what shape.

plugins.name: mycrew-chief
plugins.description: Layer 4/5 — your deputy over the whole product, as a command for one move and as a character for a whole session. /chief reads the plane, breaks an approved feature into per-repo assignments, sequences them provider-first, dispatches the worker it ships as subagents, and takes or sends back what comes home. It never decides what the product should do, and never writes code. It conducts; the workers build.

plugins.name: mycrew-warden
plugins.description: Layer 5/5 — the watch, above the chief. Start a session as @warden and it sees every other session in the project: at each trigger it asks whether the work still serves what you asked for, takes your own corrections as standing rules, stops what wandered and puts it through /why-do-it, and comes to you only with what the gate could not settle. /warden-stop and /warden-start put the watch down and pick it up without losing the session. Every trigger leaves a line on disk, so the whole watch reads back afterwards. It judges and stops; it never does the work and never says how.
